+"""Record preparation steps.
+
+``prepare_with`` validates and normalizes a record and applies a display
+transform to its value; ``prepare`` uses click short-help condensing.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import typing as t
+
+from click.utils import make_default_short_help
+
+SHORT_HELP_MAX_LENGTH = 20
+
+
+def short_help(value: str, max_length: int = SHORT_HELP_MAX_LENGTH) -> str:
+    """Condense help text with click default short-help semantics."""
+    return make_default_short_help(value, max_length)
+
+
+def validate_record(record: t.Any) -> tuple[str, t.Any, bool]:
+    """Validate ``record`` and return its trimmed key, value and enabled flag."""
+    if not isinstance(record, dict):
+        raise ValueError("record must be a dict")
+
+    key = record.get("key")
+
+    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
+        raise ValueError("record key must be a nonempty string")
+
+    if "value" not in record:
+        raise ValueError("record must have a value")
+
+    enabled = record.get("enabled", True)
+
+    if not isinstance(enabled, bool):
+        raise ValueError("record enabled must be a bool")
+
+    return key.strip(), record["value"], enabled
+
+
+def prepare_with(
+    record: t.Any, display: t.Callable[[t.Any], t.Any]
+) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
+    """Return a new prepared record whose display is ``display(value)``."""
+    key, value, enabled = validate_record(record)
+    return {
+        "key": key,
+        "value": value,
+        "display": display(value),
+        "enabled": enabled,
+    }
+
+
+def prepare(record: t.Any) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
+    """Prepare ``record`` with a short-help display of its value."""
+    return prepare_with(record, short_help)

 def prepare(record: t.Any) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
     """Prepare ``record`` with a short-help display of its value."""
     return prepare_with(record, short_help)
+
+
+def batch(records: t.Any) -> list[dict[str, t.Any]]:
+    """Prepare ``records`` in order, rejecting duplicate trimmed keys."""
+    if not isinstance(records, list):
+        raise ValueError("records must be a list")
+
+    prepared = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+
+    for record in records:
+        item = prepare(record)
+        key = item["key"]
+
+        if key in seen:
+            raise ValueError(f"duplicate record key: {key!r}")
+
+        seen.add(key)
+        prepared.append(item)
+
+    return prepared
